scenes.caption: A skinny guy walked into the gym. / Everyone was stronger.
He tried the heavy bar. / It didn't move.
They made it look effortless. / He headed for the exit.
Then he noticed a tiny dumbbell. / Almost embarrassingly easy.
So he came back. / A little heavier every time.
The same bar. One deep breath. / Nobody cheered. He simply smiled.
YOU DON'T HAVE TO BE STRONG TO START. / YOU START TO BECOME STRONG.

title: You Can Care Without Carrying Everything

scenes.caption: He was already struggling. / They handed him more.
He carried everyone's burdens. / He didn't want to disappoint them.
Every time someone asked, / he said yes.
But helping everyone / was wearing him down.
This time, he said no. / They could carry their own.
He still cared. / He just needed a limit.
YOU CAN CARE / WITHOUT CARRYING EVERYTHING.
One more favor. / He could barely stand.
He needed a break. / But he kept saying yes.
Even when he was exhausted.
This time, he noticed / what it was costing him.
They weren't happy. / He let them be disappointed.
He finally gave himself a break. / YOU'RE ALLOWED TO HAVE LIMITS.
His legs were shaking. / Then they gave out.
He looked ahead. / No finish line in sight.
Exhausted, he sat down. / And closed his eyes.
Just beyond that hill... / only a few steps away.
He couldn't see it. / But he stood up anyway.
One step. Then another. / There it was.
YOU CAN'T ALWAYS SEE / HOW CLOSE YOU ARE.
The sign said he was close. / All he could see was more road.
His legs began to shake. / He fell. Got up. Fell again.
Defeated, he sat down. / Ready to give up.
Just beyond the hill... / He had no idea how close he was.
He looked at his trembling hands. / Then slowly pushed himself up.
This time, he didn't run. / One step. Then another...
There it was. / He smiled.
YOU CAN'T ALWAYS SEE HOW CLOSE YOU ARE. / KEEP GOING.
They looked back and laughed. / He was way behind.
He tried to catch up. / He tripped and fell.
The next morning, he came back. / He ran. And fell again.
Days passed. / But every morning, he returned.
One day, the two came back. / They started running.
Suddenly, someone passed them. / The same skinny stickman.
Only now, / he didn't even look back.
DISCIPLINE MAKES NO NOISE. / RESULTS DO.
